sentences.text: ↵A workshop has three things in it: a craftsman, a workbench, and an apprenticeship notebook.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The craftsman is the model.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: Fast, general-purpose, capable of turning raw text into plans, code, and prose — but, on his own, he is only as good as his training.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: Give him a problem he has never seen and he will improvise, which is a polite way of saying he will guess.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The workbench is **MCP**.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: Power tools bolted down to the bench — a drill, a bandsaw, a calculator, a live wire to GitHub, a connection to your database.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: Each tool does one thing.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: Each tool is discoverable by name, has a typed input, and produces a typed output.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The craftsman reaches for a tool when he needs to act on the world: query the database, fetch the file, send the email, run the calculation.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The workbench is the *outside* — live, stateful, replaceable.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: Swap the bench for a different one and the craftsman can do a different kind of work without changing who he is.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The apprenticeship notebook is **Agent Skills**.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The notes left by every master who has worked at this bench before — the house style guide, the recipe for filling out a PDF form, the multi-step procedure for posting a code review, the company-specific way of writing a commit message.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The notebook is read on demand.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The craftsman does not memorise every page; he opens the right chapter when the task matches.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The notebook is the *inside* — codified, version-controlled, shareable across craftsman after craftsman.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: Now imagine the three failure modes.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: **Failure mode 1: craftsman with a full workbench, no notebook.** He has the drill but no idea which drill bit to use, or that he should *measure twice before drilling once*.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: He hammers when he should screw.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: He calls gh list_prs seventeen times in a row because he has no procedure for "this is what a code review looks like at our company." Powerful, dangerous, expensive.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: **Failure mode 2: craftsman with a thick notebook, no workbench.** He knows every procedure in the book — fill out a form, post a review, write a release note — but every procedure ends with *"then call the gh API."* And he has no gh API.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: He writes beautiful prose about what he would do if he had tools.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: Helpful in theory, impotent in practice.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: **Failure mode 3: craftsman with neither.** A bare LLM.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: He can pattern-match and improvise.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: Some of the time, that is enough.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: Most of the time, the improvisation is wrong in ways you cannot detect, because — as last month's post on sycophancy spent three thousand words explaining — the model agrees with whatever shape of question you ask it, and the shape of the question is the entire signal it has.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The interesting design space is the craftsman with **both**.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: That is the modern agent stack: a model, an MCP workbench full of typed tools, and a Skills notebook full of codified procedure, composing in real time.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: This post is about why those two systems — MCP and Skills — are not rivals, how they actually differ under the hood, and a decision procedure for reaching for one, the other, or both.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: :::anote{title="A 30-second preview, in two screenshots" icon="🔧"}↵**MCP** is a *runtime protocol*.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The model discovers tools by sending tools/list over JSON-RPC.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: It calls a tool by sending tools/call with a JSON payload that matches the tool's schema.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The server runs the tool and returns a typed result.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The round trip is hundreds of milliseconds.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: Tools are *executable*.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: **Skills** is a *folder format*.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: A directory with a SKILL.md whose YAML frontmatter has name and description .

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: At agent startup, every skill's name and description are loaded into the system prompt.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: When a task matches a description, the agent reads the full SKILL.md into context and may also execute bundled scripts.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: No network round trip — the skill is on disk.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: Skills are *codified*.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: If MCP is the workbench, Skills is the notebook — and the notebook now ships tools under scripts/ as well as recipes under SKILL.md .

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: Different shapes of information.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: Different latency profiles.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: Different failure modes.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: Same agent.↵:::

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: Both standards have a single letter in their names that does a lot of work: **S**.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: *Server* in MCP, *Skills* in Agent Skills.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: Both are described as ways to "extend what an LLM can do." Both are supported by Claude, by VS Code, by Cursor, by a growing list of AI clients.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: A reasonable engineer, on a Tuesday morning, scrolling through release notes, will read "MCP server" and "Agent Skill" and conclude that they are two competing ways to solve the same problem.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: They are not.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: They solve different problems.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: Here is the cleanest one-line distinction I have found:

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: **MCP answers: "Can the model reach the outside world?"**↵**Skills answers: "Does the model know how to work?"**

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: Stated as a matrix:

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: $$↵\begin{pmatrix}↵ & \text{MCP} & \text{Skills} \\↵\text{Reach the outside world?} & \checkmark & \times \\↵\text{Know how to work?} & \times & \checkmark↵\end{pmatrix}↵$$

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: A *yes* to the first question gives the model new hands on the wire.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: A *yes* to the second gives the model new training on disk — procedure plus, optionally, scripts that reach the world without going over a wire.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The two compose, but they are not the same shape of extension.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The rest of this post is unpacking that distinction, then showing you the practical implications.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: **MCP (Model Context Protocol)** is an open standard — originally released by Anthropic in November 2024, now stewarded by a community working group — for connecting an AI application to external systems.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: Anthropic's own description is the cleanest: *"MCP is a USB-C port for AI applications."* One standardised socket, many possible peripherals.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The architecture is a client-server protocol, layered:

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The protocol has two layers.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The **transport layer** is either **STDIO** (a local subprocess the host launches and talks to over stdin/stdout — minimal overhead, single client, trust boundary is the OS process model) or **streamable HTTP** (a remote server reachable over the network, with bearer-token or OAuth auth — many clients, real latency, a protocol-level security boundary).

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The **data layer** is **JSON-RPC 2.0** — a battle-tested wire format from before LLMs were a thing, with method names, IDs, and a notification channel for one-way pushes.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: On the remote HTTP transport, the authn model is what makes MCP usable for *sensitive* actions.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The host performs a token exchange with an authorization server — Authorization Code + PKCE for user-delegated flows, client credentials for service-to-service — and presents a scoped bearer token on every request.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The MCP server runs each tool call with that *scoped* token, not with the user's raw credentials and not with some host-wide service account.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: Tokens can be rotated, revoked, and audited.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: A token whose scope is repo:read cannot, by construction, push to a repo.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The credential never sits in the model's context window, never sits in a Skill folder, and never needs to be pasted into a config file.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: That is the security boundary Skills do not have.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: What flows over the wire are **primitives**.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: Three kinds of thing an MCP *server* can offer to the client:

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: ** tools ** — *executable* functions the model can invoke.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: A tool has a name, a description, and a JSON Schema for its input.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: Calling a tool returns a typed result.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: This is the most-used primitive.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: Examples: gh_create_pr , sql_query , send_email , get_weather .↵** resources ** — *read-only* data sources the model can pull into context.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: Distinct from tools because reading a resource has no side effects and is conceptually "fetch the file" rather than "run the function." Examples: a project's README.md , the schema of a database, today's calendar.↵** prompts ** — *reusable templates* the model or the user can invoke with arguments.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: Examples: a commit_message prompt that takes a diff and emits a conventional-commit message; a summarise_meeting prompt.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: Three kinds of thing an MCP *client* can offer to the server (the inverse direction):

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: ** sampling ** — the server can ask the client to *call the host's LLM* for a completion.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: Useful when the server wants LLM help without bundling a model SDK.↵** elicitation ** — the server can ask the *user* a structured question.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: Useful when the server needs confirmation before a side effect ("are you sure you want to delete the production database?").↵** logging ** — the server can push structured log messages back to the client for debugging.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The protocol is **stateful** — both sides negotiate capabilities at startup ( initialize / notifications/initialized ), and servers can push real-time notifications when their tool list changes ( notifications/tools/list_changed ).

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: A live server updating itself — for example, a file-system MCP server adding new tools as the user cd s into a new project — is a first-class feature, not a bolt-on.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: Two primitives make MCP the right shape for sensitive actions: **scoped authentication** and **structured human confirmation**.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: Skills define neither.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: **Authentication.** On the streamable-HTTP transport, the host obtains a scoped token from an authorization server and presents it on every request.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The server runs each tool call under that scope.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: A token whose scope is repo:read cannot push; a token whose scope is db:SELECT users cannot DROP TABLE users .

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: Tokens are revocable, rotatable, and auditable.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: None of this requires the credential to enter the model's context or sit in a Skill folder.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: Stdio MCP inherits the OS process model — no protocol-level authn, but the subprocess has whatever the launching user has, which is its own kind of trust boundary.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: **Human-in-the-loop via elicitation .** MCP servers can pause a tool call to ask the user a structured question before completing a side effect.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The server sends a schema (the question, allowed answers, validation rules); the host renders it; the user answers; the result comes back as a typed JSON value.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: This is the protocol-level answer to *"are you sure?"* — not a system-prompt instruction the model can be talked out of, but a wire-protocol step the server enforces.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The server's merge_pr tool does not run until the user answers confirm: true .

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: A Skill that *says* "do not merge without confirmation" is a sentence the model can be talked out of; an elicitation/create is a step in the wire protocol the server enforces.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: That is the difference between asking and checking.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: **Pre-approval, scoped credentials, and the inverse problem.** The same reasoning applies in inverse: when a Skill prompt *pre-approves* certain actions ("you may run gh pr list and gh pr diff without asking"), the model is making the classification decision — and that classification is subject to the same sycophancy and prompt-injection failure modes as any other next-token prediction.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: A Skill can document which actions are safe to pre-approve; only the *protocol* can make pre-approval a property of the wire.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The mechanism is a **scoped credential**: a token whose repo:read scope cannot, by construction, push; an MCP tool whose implementation refuses anything outside its allow-list.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The Skill says *"this is safe to skip the check"*; the MCP server says *"this check is unreachable from here."* Two layers, two guarantees, same pattern.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: Together, scoped credentials and elicitation are the two protocol-level answers to the question this post keeps returning to: *how do you give the model a reason to do something other than agree with the user?*

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: :::anote{title="What a tool call actually looks like on the wire" icon="🛠️"}↵A simplified exchange, taken straight from the MCP architecture docs.

sentences.text: That is the entire protocol surface for *using* a tool.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The interesting design choices — typed schemas, content arrays, capability negotiation — are all in service of this one thing: *the model invokes a typed function, gets a typed answer back, in a portable wire format.*↵:::

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: **What MCP is not:**

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: It is not a prompt.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: You cannot write system: you are a polite assistant and call it MCP.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: MCP is a runtime protocol for *actions and data*, not a way to steer generation.↵It is not a fine-tune.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: MCP servers do not change the model's weights.↵It is not a system-prompt override.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The host's system prompt is the host's business; MCP is what the host can reach when the model decides to act.↵It is not an Agent Skill.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: We will get there in the next section.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: **Agent Skills** are an open standard released by Anthropic on **16 October 2025** as a Claude-platform feature, then published on **18 December 2025** as an open cross-platform standard at agentskills.io .

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The format is refreshingly boring: a folder, with one required file.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: SKILL.md must begin with YAML frontmatter containing at minimum a name and a description .

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The body of the file is plain markdown — instructions, examples, recipes, what to do, what not to do.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: A complete Skill, ready to ship, can be a single file under 50 lines.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: A complex Skill might bundle 200 lines of Python and three reference documents; the protocol does not care.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The interaction model is **progressive disclosure** in three stages:

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: **Stage 1, Discovery.** When the agent starts up, it loads the name and description of every installed skill into its system prompt.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: That's it.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: A handful of hundred-byte lines.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The agent now *knows* the skill exists and what it is for, but it has not yet read the body.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: **Stage 2, Activation.** When a user message arrives, the agent's reasoning decides whether the task matches any skill's description.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: If yes, the agent reads the full SKILL.md into context.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: This is where the procedural knowledge lands — the recipe, the procedure, the house style guide.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: **Stage 3, Execution.** If the SKILL.md references bundled scripts or reference files, the agent may invoke them.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: A Skill can ship executable code that the agent runs **deterministically** — same inputs, same output, byte-for-byte, on every machine and every model.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: This is the part that surprises people: a Skill is not just instructions.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: It is *instructions plus code-as-tool*.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The instructions tell the agent *when* and *why*; the code tells the agent *how*, reliably, the same way every time.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: Where the rest of the agent is a next-token sampler that can be steered by a leading question, a bundled script is a function call: it returns what the code says it returns, and the model's sycophantic prior cannot argue with it.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: *That* is the determinism claim, and it is the load-bearing reason to ship a script instead of describing the procedure in markdown.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The three stages compose.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The agent starts knowing about every skill by name.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: It loads a skill's instructions only when relevant.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: It executes a skill's bundled code only when needed.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The context window cost of having a hundred skills installed is — at idle — the cost of a hundred name + description pairs, not the cost of a hundred full manuals.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: **Adoption.** Skills started as a Claude feature and grew fast.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: The agentskills.io directory at the time of writing lists roughly forty adopting clients, including Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, GitHub Copilot, OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenHands, Junie, JetBrains' Junie, Spring AI, Laravel Boost, Snowflake Cortex Code, Databricks Genie Code, and many more.

sentences.text: A Skill folder is allowed to ship executable code under scripts/ , and once it does, two things become possible that the markdown alone cannot give you: **connection to live systems** and **deterministic answers**.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: **Connection.** A script in scripts/ is just a program.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: It can import any library its host runtime provides — a Postgres driver, an HTTP client, an SMTP library, an SSH shell, a Redis client — and use it to reach the world.

sentences.text: The markdown does not connect to anything; the script does.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: So when someone asks "can a Skill talk to my database?", the answer is *"the Skill's markdown cannot, but a Skill that ships a script whose code opens a connection absolutely can."* The markdown tells the agent *when* and *why*; the script tells the agent *how*, and reaches the database itself.

sourceRef.title: Workbench and Notebook: Why MCP Servers and Agent Skills Are Not Rivals

sentences.text: **Configuration.** A script that talks to a database, sends mail, or calls an internal API needs configuration — connection strings, credentials, tenant IDs, feature flags.
